moments.title: Grant Park Stadium opens
moments.text: The colonnaded lakefront stadium opened as Municipal Grant Park Stadium. It was renamed Soldier Field in 1925 as a memorial to American soldiers of World War I.

moments.title: Dedicated at the Army-Navy game
moments.text: The stadium was formally dedicated during an Army-Navy football game that ended in a 21 to 21 tie before a huge crowd.

moments.title: The "long count" fight
moments.text: More than 100,000 people watched Gene Tunney beat Jack Dempsey. Tunney was knocked down in the seventh round, but the count was delayed while Dempsey went to a neutral corner.

moments.title: King's Chicago Freedom Movement rally
moments.text: Martin Luther King Jr. spoke to a crowd estimated at 30,000 to 65,000, then led a march to City Hall, where he posted demands for an open city.

moments.title: The Bears move in
moments.text: After about 50 years at Wrigley Field, the Chicago Bears made Soldier Field their home.

moments.title: A new stadium inside the old one
moments.text: A rebuilt stadium opened with a modern glass-and-steel seating bowl set inside the 1920s colonnades. In 2006 the change cost the stadium its National Historic Landmark status.

moments.title: Today: home of the Bears
moments.text: The Bears still play at Soldier Field, and the original colonnades still line the lakefront.

facts.label: Long count crowd
facts.note: Counts range from 104,943 to well over 120,000.

facts.label: King rally crowd
facts.note: Press reports at the time differed widely.

facts.label: Landmark status
facts.note: National Historic Landmark designation was withdrawn on Feb 17, 2006.

sources.title: Grant Park Stadium (Soldier Field) (National Park Service)

checked.notes: Built 1924, renamed Soldier Field 1925, dedicated Nov 27, 1926 (Britannica). Long count Sept 22, 1927; attendance is disputed (104,943 to over 120,000), so the story now says 'more than 100,000' instead of 'about 100,000'. King's July 10, 1966 rally confirmed; crowd estimates range from 30,000 to 65,000. Bears from 1971 (Britannica). Rebuilt stadium opened Sept 29, 2003; NHL designation withdrawn Feb 17, 2006 (NPS). The original name Municipal Grant Park Stadium follows the NPS listing name and general accounts.
